title: The Trapdoor
build: Cleveland Cracking Service disk, cracked by Ian

tools.emulator: VICE MCP v3.14.0 macOS arm64 headless, dummy audio

exclude: Blank crack-intro screen cells, all $20 from the SYS stop through early play.
VIC bitmap output. A store watch at $FD30 stopped in the startup clear loop at $6272. The apparent copy of KERNAL vectors there predates unpacking.
Zero at entry. Generated message and drawing workspace cleared at $57DC–$57E2. A store watch on the last two pages caught $57DF with the CPU port at $30.
The runtime vector block is initialised from the eight authored bytes at $3959. A store watch caught the first write at $38D5 with X=$07.
Zero fill introduced by the disk expansion. A write watch from cassette LOAD through the original hand-off at $3800 recorded zero writes, and this interval retained its power-on contents.
Zero fill introduced by the disk expansion. On the original cassette a write watch was silent through $3800 while the separate watch at $9600 caught STA ($FB),Y at $03C0.

CPU port and runtime zero-page state with no code in the hand-off. The game copies its initial state from the authored template at $C508 to $0010–$0077 with $3F69/$3F6C. Other zero-page values are loader state or scratch.

Text screen residue at hand-off and generated sound workspace during gameplay. A first-access watch caught the $0404 screen byte read at $5EE9, then the first write from $5EEF. The two loops fill $0400–$0599 with zero before restoring the screen byte used as initial SID volume and mode. $059A holds an effect header field and $059B/$059C hold the saved Timer B hook, both installed by code.
extra: Expanded disk payload reproduced from the packed PRG. The original cassette write watches distinguish the two disk zero-fill ranges from the cassette payload.

io: Both clearing loops run with the CPU port set to $30 by their callers.
The glyph printer uses $31 to read character ROM when selected and writes the bitmap and style state in RAM.
